title: SpaceBan/set has no 'ban' permission enforcement
description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/ban.rs:85-364 (handle_ban_set). MemoryBackend generic create_object<SpaceBan>/update_object<SpaceBan>/destroy_object<SpaceBan> in src/memory.rs all perform zero permission check.

draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §SpaceBan/set (lines 1310-1318):
- 'create accepts: spaceId (String, required), userId (String, required), reason (String, optional), expiresAt (UTCDate, optional). **Requires `"ban"` permission in the Space.**'
- 'destroy lifts the ban. Requires `"ban"` permission in the Space.'

The kit has no `"ban"` permission string analogous to MANAGE_SPACE/MANAGE_ROLES/MANAGE_MEMBERS/MANAGE_CHANNELS in src/permissions.rs. No required_permissions_for_op analog for SpaceBan ops. The handler does no defense-in-depth pre-check.

Trigger: any non-privileged member of a Space can ban any other member (or even non-members) by issuing SpaceBan/set create. This is a privilege-escalation vector that lets a single compromised low-privilege account remove arbitrary members.

Fix sketch:
1. Add BAN permission constant to src/permissions.rs.
2. Add ChatBackend::create_space_ban/destroy_space_ban methods (or reuse the apply_space_patch pattern with new variants) that gate atomically.
3. Reference MemoryBackend implements the gate via member_effective_permissions inside the new method, mirroring the apply_space_patch_impl pre-validation pattern.
close_reason: Fixed by later work: ban.rs:234/314/377 call backend.may_set_space_ban before create/update/destroy; MemoryBackend memory.rs:1309-1333 requires permissions::BAN. Verified 2026-10-19: tests/space_ban_permissions.rs create/update/destroy_requires_ban_permission pass (3/3).
